title: Descent of degree-minus-one graded maps on bounded finitely presented complexes
statement: Let I be a directed preorder and F a diagram of commutative rings with colimit A [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix i₀ in I, and cochain complexes E₀ and K₀ of F(i₀)-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Assume E₀ is zero outside a finite interval and every term of E₀ and K₀ is finitely presented [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Write Eᵢ and Kᵢ for their termwise scalar extensions to a stage i at least i₀, and E and K for their extensions to A. Given such a stage i and a degree-minus-one graded family s, consisting of a map Eⁿ to Kⁿ⁻¹ for every integer n, there exist j at least i and a degree-minus-one family t between Eⱼ and Kⱼ whose scalar extension to A agrees componentwise with s. The scalar extension uses the same canonical associativity transport as [def-pc-complex-scalar-extension-hom]; its left and right comparison maps L and R are given explicitly in lean.statement. No chain-map or homotopy identity is imposed.

proof.text: For each degree m in a finite support interval of E₀, apply the maps clause of finite-presentation descent to E₀.X m and K₀.X (m-1). Choose a common upper stage also above i. For a preorder, quotient by mutual comparability and choose representatives. This is an equivalent indexing category; F sends equivalent indices to inverse ring isomorphisms. Use finite-presentation descent on that partial-order diagram and transport back, enlarging above the requested original i. Equivalently the coefficient-matrix proof uses the elementwise filtered-colimit criterion and only directedness.

Transport every descended component to the common stage by scalar-extension associativity. The comparison isomorphisms in the finite-presentation theorem send 1 tensor x to 1 tensor (1 tensor x). These are exactly the values of extendScalarsComp, so tensor generation identifies the comparisons with the displayed L and R, after the ring-homomorphism equality hc. Put zero outside the finite source interval; extension of scalars preserves these zero source terms. The up-shape relation n to m forces n=m-1, so this defines every required component and proves its equality to s after extension.

lean.statement:
theorem affine_perfect_gradedHom_descent
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (i₀ : I)
    (E₀ K₀ : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (F.obj i₀)) ℤ)
    (hbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (E₀.X n))
    (hEfp : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.FinitePresentation (F.obj i₀) (E₀.X n))
    (hKfp : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.FinitePresentation (F.obj i₀) (K₀.X n))
    (i : Set.Ici i₀)
    (s : ∀ m n : ℤ, (ComplexShape.up ℤ).Rel n m →
      ((((ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F i₀).hom).mapHomologicalComplex
      (.up ℤ)).obj E₀).X m ⟶ (((ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F i₀).hom).mapHomologicalComplex
      (.up ℤ)).obj K₀).X n)) :
    ∃ (j : Set.Ici i₀) (hij : i ≤ j)
      (t : ∀ m n : ℤ, (ComplexShape.up ℤ).Rel n m →
        ((((ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE j.property)).hom).mapHomologicalComplex
          (.up ℤ)).obj E₀).X m ⟶
          (((ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE j.property)).hom).mapHomologicalComplex
          (.up ℤ)).obj K₀).X n)),
      let hc := congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom
        (colimit.w F (homOfLE j.property)).symm
      let L := eqToHom (congrArg (fun r ↦
          ((ModuleCat.extendScalars r).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj E₀) hc) ≫
        (NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.extendScalarsComp
          (F.map (homOfLE j.property)).hom (colimit.ι F j.val).hom) (.up ℤ)).hom.app E₀
      let R := (NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.extendScalarsComp
          (F.map (homOfLE j.property)).hom (colimit.ι F j.val).hom) (.up ℤ)).inv.app K₀ ≫
        eqToHom (congrArg (fun r ↦
          ((ModuleCat.extendScalars r).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K₀) hc.symm)
      ∀ m n : ℤ, ∀ hmn : (ComplexShape.up ℤ).Rel n m,
        L.f m ≫ (ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F j.val).hom).map (t m n hmn) ≫
          R.f n = s m n hmn
